stemMarkdown: A train 285 m long travelling at 45 km/h overtakes a man walking at 3.6 km/h in the same direction as the train. How many seconds does the train take to pass him completely? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Same direction, so the speeds subtract: $45 - 3.6 = 41.4$ km/h $= 11.5000$ m/s. The train covers its own length relative to the man: $\dfrac{285}{11.5000} = 24.7826$ seconds.
altSolutionMarkdown: A man is treated as having no length — only the train's length counts.
